answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to continuously cultivate a private computational orchard of verifiable micro-tasks whose outputs are hashed into a shared ledger. Attackers must expend real energy and specialized hardware for every fake node because the orchard only accepts work submitted through a narrow, rate-limited inlet; cheaply cloned agents lack the sable resource stream needed to keep their trees productive, so mass fakes collapse under the accumulating cost of sustained proof generation.
